cite: SRD 5.2.1, Core Bard Traits; Spellcasting (Bard); Bard Subclass; Ability Score Improvement; Epic Boon
note: Task 11 (phase 4 plan 12): new overlay, class 1->20. Core Bard Traits (vendored srd-2024_bard_core-traits): "Hit Point Die: D8"; "Saving Throw Proficiencies: Dexterity and Charisma" (upstream saving_throws [cha, dex], correct as vendored); "Skill Proficiencies: Choose any 3 skills" -- the transform already seeds skillChoice.from with all 18 skills (count 0 placeholder), so only count:3 changes (the full 18-slug list is restated because `set` replaces the whole object); "Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons"; "Armor Training: Light armor". "Tool Proficiencies: Choose 3 Musical Instruments" is NOT representable: ClassEntity.toolProficiencies is a fixed list of tool ids (monk precedent: no tool choice shape) -- left [], flagged for the owner (the character sheet's tools are free-noted). Cantrips column (vendored srd-2024_bard_cantrips: 2 at levels 1-3, 3 at 4-9, 4 at 10-20): transformClasses() auto-carries it under extra['bard-cantrips'], which is NOT the key packages/engine/src/derive/spellcasting.ts reads (cantripsKnownKey('bard') = 'bard-cantrips-known'), so levels 1/4/10 author the explicit correctly-keyed extra (2/3/4) alongside the harmless unread auto key (wizard precedent). bestRowExtra picks the highest row at or below the character's level, so three breakpoints cover all 20 levels. Prepared Spells column (4,5,6,7,9,10,11,12,14,15,16,16,17,17,18,18,19,20,21,22; verified level-by-level against every vendored srd-2024_bard_prepared-spells row) is carried verbatim under extra['bard-prepared-spells'] == preparedSpellsKey('bard'): zero authoring. Spell Slots 1st-9th columns ride on the rows as extras; slot rows used by derive come from the system 'full' table, cross-checked against the vendored columns by a derive-level test. Bardic Die column (D6/D8/D10/D12) rides as an untouched display-only text extra (ruling 1). Bard Subclass @3 (College of Lore is the only SRD subclass); ASI @4/8/12/16 and Epic Boon @19 use the standard open feat pick (Fighter/Wizard shape; vendored text: 'or another feat of your choice for which you qualify').

SRD text: Charisma is the spellcasting ability; prepared spells of level 1+ from the Bard list (count from the Prepared Spells column); "You can use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus" (focus:true); full-caster slots (system 'full' table). NO ritual casting is granted by the vendored Bard text (unlike Wizard/Cleric/Druid), so ritual:false. No cantripsKnown/preparedCount formulas: both counts are read from the class rows' extras (see class/bard's note), which is exact for all 20 levels.

SRD text: "You can confer a Bardic Inspiration die a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest." Granted at Bard level 1. Fully expressible: resource.define 'bardic-inspiration' max 'max(1, mod(cha))' reset longRest plus action.define{kind:'bonus', resource}. The die size (d6, d8@5, d10@10, d12@15) is the Bardic Die column, display-only text on the class rows (ruling 1; no engine reader). RESET-BY-LEVEL FINDING: Font of Inspiration (level 5) changes the reset to Short OR Long Rest, but redefining the same resource id at a later level CANNOT change it -- packages/engine/src/derive/resources.ts stacks max via a sum-unique-key table (higher wins) but takes name/reset/display from the FIRST effect encountered (`if (!meta.has(eff.id))`), so a second define from the level-5 feature would never override the level-1 longRest. The reset therefore stays longRest at every level and Font of Inspiration is a text feature (see its entry); a character who regains uses on a short rest tracks that by hand. Flagged: slice-3 vocabulary candidate (a resource whose reset can be upgraded by a later define, or a per-level reset).

effects.name: Bardic Inspiration
effects.description: Inspire another creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice (a creature can have only one at a time). Once within the next hour when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. The die is expended when it's rolled. The die is a d6, becoming a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15 (see the Bardic Die column).

note: SRD text: "You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest. In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration." Granted at Bard level 5. TEXT FALLBACK + FLAG. Two halves, both inexpressible: (1) the short-rest reset -- see feature/bard-bardic-inspiration's RESET-BY-LEVEL FINDING (a later resource.define cannot replace the first define's reset; the resource stays longRest); (2) "expend a spell slot to regain one use" is a cross-pool conversion (slot counter -> resource counter) with no effect type. Text-feature fallback per ruling 9's bar.

effects.name: Font of Inspiration
effects.description:
You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest. (Tracked on the sheet as a Long Rest pool: reset the uses by hand after a Short Rest.)

In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.

note: SRD text: "You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus." Granted at Bard level 2. FULLY EXPRESSIBLE (registry check, ruling 5): ProficiencyLevelSchema has 'half', and the engine resolves it BENEATH proficient/expertise (proficiency.ts proficiencyLevel: expertise > proficient > half; proficiencyAmount floors prof*0.5), so a skill the bard is (or later becomes) proficient in stays at full proficiency and only lacking skills get the floor-halved bonus. One proficiency.grant{kind:'skill', level:'half'} per system skill (18; targets are the skill slugs, same keys as skillChoice.from) -- the grants are fixed ids, which is exactly right here because the rule applies to ALL skills. Derive-level tests pin the totals at +2/+3/+4/+5/+6 proficiency (half = 1/1/2/2/3) and that proficient skills are unchanged. Scope note: the SRD wording is every skill-proficiency-lacking ability check, i.e. the 18 skills; Initiative (a Dexterity check with no skill) and bare ability checks are not covered by a skill-level grant -- the engine has no hook for those, so they are the one residual gap (table-resolved).

SRD text: "You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice... At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice." Granted at Bard levels 2 and 9. TEXT FALLBACK + OWNER-FLAG (same registry check as Rogue/Ranger): proficiency.grant{level:'expertise'} exists but its `target` is a FIXED authored string, so it cannot express "two skills of the character's choice"; the only per-selection mechanism is a skill-typed pick, which (since plan 12 task 5) grants BASE proficiency -- authoring Expertise as a pick would GRANT proficiency (state-wrong), the forbidden shape, so NO choice and NO proficiency.grant is authored (a test pins feature.text only). Slice-3 vocabulary candidate: a pick whose selections apply proficiency.grant{level:'expertise'} to chosen skills the character is already proficient in.

effects.name: Expertise
effects.description:
You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Performance and Persuasion are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

note: SRD text: "If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has Advantage." Granted at Bard level 7. Inexpressible: a reaction that forces a reroll of another creature's failed save with Advantage -- no reroll/advantage-on-reroll vocabulary (advantage.grant is a standing grant, not a one-shot on a rerolled save). Text-feature fallback per ruling 9's bar; flagged.

effects.name: Countercharm
effects.description: You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has Advantage.

note: SRD text: whenever the Prepared Spells number increases (from level 10 on), the new prepared spells may be chosen from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard lists and count as Bard spells; replacements may come from those lists too. Granted at Bard level 10. Inexpressible honestly: spell.listAdd adds a FIXED id list to the class list unconditionally (it would put ~300 cleric/druid/wizard spells on the bard list for every pick, including the pre-10 prepared spells and replacements the rule keeps Bard-only), and spellcasting.define.list is a single class ref or fixed id list with no 'extra lists from level N, for new picks only' shape. Text-feature fallback per ruling 9's bar; flagged (slice-3 vocabulary candidate: a level-gated, additive spell-list source).

effects.name: Magical Secrets
effects.description: You've learned secrets from various magical traditions. Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number in the Bard Features table increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard spell lists, and the chosen spells count as Bard spells for you. In addition, whenever you replace a spell prepared for this class, you can replace it with a spell from those lists.

note: SRD text: "When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that." Granted at Bard level 18. Inexpressible: an Initiative-triggered partial refill of a resource -- resource resets are rest-based only, with no roll-triggered 'top up to N' semantics. Text-feature fallback per ruling 9's bar; flagged.

effects.name: Superior Inspiration
effects.description: When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

note: SRD text: "You always have the Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill spells prepared. When you cast either spell, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target." Granted at Bard level 20. The always-prepared half is two spell.grant{alwaysPrepared:true} (both spells exist in the pack; always-prepared spells don't count against the prepared cap, matching the vendored Spellcasting text). The second-target rider is a per-cast spell-targeting modifier with no vocabulary, so it rides as a feature.text; flagged.

effects.name: Words of Creation
effects.description: When you cast Power Word Heal or Power Word Kill, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target.

cite: SRD 5.2.1, College of Lore — Bonus Proficiencies
note: SRD text: "You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice." Granted at Bard level 3 (Lore level 3). A count-3 skill-typed query pick on the subclass's own level-3 row -- LEGAL and correct here (unlike Expertise): since plan 12 task 5 the engine grants BASE proficiency for any decided pick of skill entities (derive/abilities.ts), which is exactly what this feature gives. Any skill is offered (including ones already proficient, where the pick is a harmless no-op: the SRD text has no 'new skill' rider). Same subclass-row shape as Champion's second fighting style; subclass-row choices surface through levelScopedChoices once the subclass is chosen at 3.

cite: SRD 5.2.1, College of Lore — Bonus Proficiencies
note: The mechanic is the count-3 skill pick on subclass/college-of-lore's level-3 row (see that entry). This feature carries a feature.text so the granted feature is not silently effect-less (ruling 9's never-silent letter); zero web-risk (an unconditional feature grant never touches the choice-surfacing path).

effects.name: Bonus Proficiencies
effects.description: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

cite: SRD 5.2.1, College of Lore — Cutting Words
note: SRD text: "When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a damage roll or succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration; roll your Bardic Inspiration die, and subtract the number rolled from the creature's roll." Granted at Lore level 3. The reaction that spends one 'bardic-inspiration' pool use is expressible as action.define{kind:'reaction', resource:'bardic-inspiration'}; the roll-subtraction on another creature's roll is narrative (no effect type).

effects.name: Cutting Words
effects.description: When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a damage roll or succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration; roll your Bardic Inspiration die, and subtract the number rolled from the creature's roll, reducing the damage or potentially turning the success into a failure.

cite: SRD 5.2.1, College of Lore — Magical Discoveries
note: SRD text: "You learn two spells of your choice. These spells can come from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list or any combination thereof... You always have the chosen spells prepared, and whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of the spells with another spell that meets these requirements." Granted at Lore level 6. Inexpressible: spell.grant targets one FIXED spell id, not a player-chosen spell from three class lists limited to levels the character has slots for, with a per-level replacement; same gap class as Magical Secrets. Text-feature fallback per ruling 9's bar; flagged.

effects.name: Magical Discoveries
effects.description: You learn two spells of your choice. These spells can come from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list or any combination thereof. A spell you choose must be a cantrip or a spell for which you have spell slots. You always have the chosen spells prepared, and whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of the spells with another spell that meets these requirements.

cite: SRD 5.2.1, College of Lore — Peerless Skill
note: SRD text: "When you make an ability check or attack roll and fail, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and add the number rolled to the d20... On a failure, the Bardic Inspiration isn't expended." Granted at Lore level 14. Inexpressible: a post-roll, conditionally-refunded add-die on the character's own failed roll -- no post-roll hook or conditional-refund vocabulary. Text-feature fallback per ruling 9's bar; flagged.

effects.name: Peerless Skill
effects.description: When you make an ability check or attack roll and fail, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning a failure into a success. On a failure, the Bardic Inspiration isn't expended.
